mathematical_definition: rolling_60_std(spread) -- standard deviation of quoted spread over a trailing 60-bar window
numerical_stability_notes: live_compatible=false: MarketState's bounded live buffer (built in an earlier phase of this project) does not retain per-bar spread history -- only the current live tick's instantaneous spread, plus small tick-level ring buffers a later, different family (Task 21) will use for live spread dynamics. There is no trailing 60-bar spread window available live to compute a rolling std over, so this feature genuinely cannot run from the live engine's bounded window as implemented; Task 21's live-tick spread family replaces it for live use (spec section 7). Naturally near-zero for long stretches given spread_constant_frac below.
missing_value_policy: NaN for first 60 bars, never zero-filled
status_reason: Not a v3 survivor (research/output/v3_feature_survivors.json): catboost_importance=0.000 (<0.3), MI rank 117 (outside top 15). catboost_importance=0.0, cv_importance=0.0, mi_rank=117, family=H_microstructure. SUMMARY.md finding #9: spread is dead weight -- zero CatBoost importance (the model never splits on it), because it is a constant for 98.9% of training history. research/historical_coverage.py's measure_coverage('data/gold_seed_merged_full6yr.csv') (freshly run 2026-08-19 against the real 2,456,224-row merged CSV): spread_constant_frac=0.9889492977839155. spread is present for the entire dataset (historical_coverage=FULL_HISTORY) but is degenerate (near-constant, hence near-zero rolling std) for almost all of it. Kept registered per spec section 9 -- Phase 4 may find it useful for a different target.
